Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of Criminal Appeal U/s 374 Cr.P.C preferred on behalf of appellant Mr. Naushad @ Raju@ Bhura against the impugned judgment dated 12.03.2022 of Ld.
MM-04, South, Saket in Criminal Case No. 4696/2018 pertaining to FIR No. 250/18, PS Sangam Vihar whereby the appellant herein was convicted for the offence Digitally CA No.225/2022 Naushad @ Raju @ Bhura Vs. The State Page 1 / 6 signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.09.18 16:39:27 +0530 U/s 380/454 IPC in plea bargaining proceedings and was sentenced to simple imprisonment for one year alongwith fine of Rs. 500/- each for both the offences.
2. Briefly stated the facts as per record are as under:-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A case FIR No. 250 was lodged at PS Sangam Vihar on 28.06.2018 for the offences U/s 457/380 IPC on the basis of written complaint of one Mr. Vimal Gupta.
It was alleged by him that theft had been committed at his house after breaking open the lock in his absence on 27.06.2018.
He had also stated about the articles stolen during said incident.

After registration of FIR, investigation was conducted and appellant herein was arrested on 28.06.2018 and some of the stolen articles were recovered Naushad@Raju@Bhura vs State on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50600629/

sentences.text: 1 from his possession
. He was charge-sheeted for the offences U/s 457/380/411 IPC.
Charge-sheet was filed before Ld. Trial Court on 08.10.2018 and cognizance thereupon was taken on 20.10.2018.
Appellant was summoned as an accused for 16.01.2019.
Thereafter, charge was framed against him for the offence U/s 457 IPC alternatively for the offence U/s 454 IPC alongwith offence U/s 380/411 IPC vide order dated 10.05.2019.
Subsequently, the offence U/s 411 IPC was compounded by the appellant with the complainant Mr. Vimal Gupta on 24.01.2020.
It was submitted on his behalf that he will approach Hon'ble High Court of Delhi for quashing of other offences.
It appears that no quashing petition was filed rather an application for plea bargaining alongwith an affidavit was filed on 02.03.2022.
The application was taken up on 08.03.2022 in pre-sitting of Lok Adalat.
Mutual Satisfactory Disposition was recorded on said date.
Thereafter, matter was taken up in Lok Adalat on 12.03.2022 whereupon the appellant was convicted for the offences U/s 380/454 IPC.

He was CA No.225/2022 Naushad @ Raju @ Bhura Vs.
The State Page 2 / 6 SUNIL GUPTA sentenced to simple imprisonment for one year alongwith fine of Rs. 500/- for offence U/s 380 IPC.

The State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, he was sentenced to simple imprisonment for one year alongwith fine of Rs. 500/- for offence U/s 454 IPC.
That order is being challenged in these proceedings.
3. No arguments have been adduced on behalf of appellant despite several opportunities.
In these circumstances, appeal is being disposed of on the basis of grounds as mentioned in the petition of appeal filed before this Court.

As per the same, the only ground taken by the appellant for assailing the impugned order is that Ld. Judge, Lok Adalat failed to appreciate that plea bargaining was not permissible for the offence U/s 454 IPC as same is punishable with imprisonment up to 10 years alongwith fine.
Prayer has been made to set aside the impugned order.
4. Ld. Addl. PP for State has submitted that present appeal is not maintainable and has prayed for dismissal of the same.
5. I have considered the appeal alongwith Trial Court record.

6. Perusal of impugned order dated 12.03.2022 shows that after convicting the appellant herein for the offences U/s 380/454 IPC, he was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment of one year alongwith fine of Rs. 500/- for both the offences separately and was taken into custody for serving the sentence.

At that stage itself, Ld. Counsel for the appellant had shown his willingness to withdraw the application for plea bargaining, may be because he was hoping that substantive imprisonment shall not be awarded to appellant in those proceedings.

His request for withdrawal of CA No.225/2022 Naushad @ Raju @ Bhura Vs. The State Page 3 / 6 Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.09.18 16:39:50 +0530 application was rightly declined by Ld. Trial Court by observing that once the proceedings of plea bargaining have been completed, the application cannot be withdrawn.

sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, only ground taken for assailing the impugned order is that the offence U/s 454 IPC for which he has been convicted, is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to 10 years so same could not have been disposed of by way of plea bargaining proceedings.

Without going into merits, Section 265G Cr.P.C. is material here which provides as under:-
"265G. Finality of the judgment.-

The judgment delivered by the Court under section 265G shall be final and no appeal (except the special leave petition under Article 136 and writ petition under articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution) shall lie in any Court against such judgment."

8. Present appeal has been filed on behalf of appellant U/s 374 Cr.P.C. which provides as under:-
"374. Appeals from convictions.-
(1) Any person convicted on a trial held by a High Court in its extraordinary original criminal jurisdiction may appeal to the Supreme Court.

(2) Any person convicted on a trial held by a Sessions Judge or an Additional Sessions Judge or on a trial held by any other Court in which a sentence of imprisonment for more than 7 years [has been passed against him or against any other person convicted at the same trial]; may appeal to the High Court.

(3) Save as otherwise provided in sub-section (2), any person,-

2023.09.18 16:40:10 +0530 (a) convicted on a trial held by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Assistant Sessions Judge or Magistrate of the first class, or of the second class, or (b) sentenced under section 325, or (c) in respect of whom an order has been made or a sentence has been passed under section 360 by any Magistrate, may appeal to the Court of Session.

(4) When an appeal has been filed against a sentence passed under section 376, section 376A,
section 376AB, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB or section 376E of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 186.), the appeal shall be disposed of within a period of six months from the date of filing of such appeal."
9.

As mentioned earlier, the appellant herein was convicted by Ld. Judge, Lok Adalat on 12.03.2022 in plea bargaining proceedings so present appeal is not maintainable in view of bar as contained in Section 265G Cr.P.C. mentioned above.

The appeal could not have been filed U/s 374 Cr.P.C. as same provides for appeal only in the cases where any person has been convicted after trial or has Naushad@Raju@Bhura vs State on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50600629/
3 been sentenced U/s 325 Cr.P.C., or an order has been passed against him or sentence has been passed U/s 360 Cr.P.C. which admittedly is not the case here.
10.
Appeal stands dismissed in above terms being not maintainable.
